source: RC-01, the seven-row reconciled budget table in docs/revamp/06-WORK-ORDERS.md §1, ratified at Gate 2 (docs/revamp/DECISIONS.md D-010)
$comment: Every ceiling here is an INTEGER NUMBER OF BYTES, never a "KB" string (WO-23 criterion 2).
scripts/route-budgets.mjs rejects anything else outright, so the comparison is unambiguous.
RC-01 prints KiB for humans; budgetLabel carries that text and is display-only.
RATCHET RULE (04-ARCHITECTURE.md §8.4): a ceiling may only move in a PR that edits this file
in the same commit and states the reason in the PR body. No environment variable and no CLI
flag skips the check -- scripts/route-budgets.mjs accepts no arguments and reads no environment,
and tests/budgets.test.ts asserts that against the script's own source text.
baselineBytes are the retained Gate 1 measurements in docs/revamp/baseline/README.md
("Bundle baseline"), reproduced by this script from the current build as its correctness proof.

method.polyfills: excluded from every JavaScript row, per RC-01 'excl. polyfill'
method.fonts: raw woff2 bytes -- woff2 is already Brotli-compressed, so file size is wire weight
method.note: zlib level 6 is not a preference: summing per-file level-6 gzip over the /c/[id] first-load union reproduces the retained baseline's 184,745 B exactly, and no other level does.
method.stability: REPEATED BUILDS OF AN UNCHANGED TREE OSCILLATE BY UNDER 10 B ON THE THREE JS ROWS (observed twice while WO-31 measured its ratchet: `/` 158,870-158,878, `/c/[id]` 182,769-182,776, shared 131,641). Content hashes appear inside the webpack runtime manifest, so a differing hash string is itself a few bytes of differing gzip input. This is why no ceiling here is set at a hairline over its measurement, and why measuredBytes in a ratchet record is the CONSERVATIVE figure of repeated builds rather than a single run's.

ratchet.pr: WO-31 -- legacy removal, the equivalence table, and the ratchet
ratchet.authority: WO-31 acceptance criterion 5: 'Budget thresholds are ratcheted down to the measured post-cleanup values, under the same ratchet rule.' Every figure below was measured by scripts/route-budgets.mjs on this branch rebased onto main at d3460a7 (PR #111). To be recorded in docs/revamp/DECISIONS.md by the coordinator.
ratchet.why: THE DELETIONS SHIPPED ALMOST NO BYTES, AND THAT IS THE FINDING RATHER THAN A DISAPPOINTMENT. Measured against WO-20's figures on the SAME main (8f0d738), `/` moves 158899 -> 158839 B (-60) and `/c/[id]` 182784 -> 182723 B (-61) across this PR; the finals below sit 39 B and 53 B above those, which is #111's cost and not this PR's. The deletions are nearly free because WO-20 had already stopped COMPOSING the nine legacy components and the bundler had already tree-shaken them -- what WO-31 removes is dead FILES, not shipped weight. So this ratchet is not banking a saving this PR made. It closes the gap between ceilings that were projected from the LEGACY surface and the finished surface that is now what ships -- the one Gate-4 moment where every row is measured against the thing it gates. 166912 B (163 KiB) is +5.1% over the measurement, holding WO-20's convention of a deliberately tighter figure than RC-01's ~8% for a row measured rather than projected. baselineBytes stays 137272 -- the retained Gate 1 figure for the LEGACY landing page -- so the report's baseline-reproduction table keeps meaning what it meant. RE-MEASURED AFTER A REBASE. This PR's first measurement was taken on main at 8f0d738; `fix/mobile-shell-cls-lcp` then merged as #111 and the finals were retaken on the rebased tree at d3460a7. That fix costs `/` +39 B, `/c/[id]` +53 B and the CSS row +17 B -- its ~33 new declarations gzip to almost nothing -- and the font row not one byte, because it changes `preload` and emits no new face. Every ceiling below already carried that movement.

previousMovement.pr: WO-20 -- ThreadTimeline, ActiveRunPanel, and the route composition
previousMovement.note: Superseded by the WO-31 ratchet above; retained because its rejected-alternative argument (the React.lazy build at 143426 B, and why page-has-heading-one beats a budget row) is the reason this row sits above RC-01's 148480 B at all, and that argument is not superseded by a smaller ceiling.
previousMovement.why: RC-01's 148480 B was +8.2% over a measured baseline of 137272 B, and that baseline is the LEGACY landing page -- QueryForm: a textarea and a button, with no counter, no billability disclosure, no normalized failure and no guarded submission path. The redesigned `/` is 03 §1.4's composer plus the job machine, and `useJobRun().submit` is the only permitted route to POST /research (R-01, H6, MUST-KEEP 3): the endpoint has no idempotency key, so the machine's submission token is what makes a duplicate response unable to buy a second run. lib/job/ therefore cannot leave the route, and the measurement on this branch is 158899 B. THE ALTERNATIVE WAS BUILT AND MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: putting the composer behind React.lazy the way ThreadRailBridge puts the rail lands `/` at 143426 B, inside the old ceiling -- and is rejected, because Next resolves a lazy boundary's FALLBACK into the prerendered HTML (verified on this build: index.html carries the rail's `data-thread-rail-state="loading"`, not its rows), so `/` would serve a document with no h1 and fail `page-has-heading-one`, which WO-22 criterion 2 gates at zero -- and the only fallback that keeps the h1 is the composer itself, whose sole refusal label is 'Generating plan…', a sentence that would be false on every first paint. Across the two routes the composition is NET NEGATIVE: 158899 + 182784 = 341683 B against main's 146447 + 199425 = 345872 B, because retiring ConversationThread takes the static react-markdown import off /c/[id]. 167936 B (164 KiB) is +5.7% over the measurement -- deliberately tighter than RC-01's ~8% convention, because this row is now measured against the finished surface rather than projected from the legacy one.

previousMovement.pr: WO-23 -- route budget check, budgets.json, and npm run budgets
previousMovement.note: Superseded by the WO-31 ratchet above; retained because it is the record of why this row exceeds RC-01's 122880 B at all -- React DOM plus the Next runtime already totalled 128973 B before any application code existed, so the RC-01 ceiling was infeasible from day one.
previousMovement.why: RC-01 set 120 KiB for this row without a measured baseline -- its own headroom column reads '-'. The first measurement, taken by this script on the main build, is 130865 B, so the ceiling was infeasible from day one: React DOM (63370 B) + the Next app-router client runtime (65603 B) already total 128973 B, which exceeds 122880 B before any application code exists. rows.label: Shared framework/runtime chunk
rows.definition: The build manifest's rootMainFiles minus polyfillFiles -- the chunk set every app route loads (webpack runtime, React DOM chunk, Next app-router client runtime, main-app). This is Next's 'First Load JS shared by all'.
rows.note: RAISED to 141312 by WO-23, then LOWERED to 139264 (136 KiB) by WO-31, both under the ratchet rule. See the shared-framework-runtime entry in budgets.ratchet and its previousMovement. baselineBytes stays null because RC-01 recorded no measured baseline for this row; the measured figures (130865 B at WO-23, 131644 B here) live in the ratchet record, not here, so the report's baseline-reproduction table keeps meaning 'reproduces the retained Gate 1 figures'.

rows.label: All self-hosted font files (woff2, latin subset)
rows.definition: Raw bytes of every emitted woff2, found in .next/static/media (next/font/local) and public/ (hand-rolled @font-face). Measured from the font binaries, never from the JS manifests (WO-23 criterion 3). Reports 0 B and is flagged as not-yet-meaningful until WO-02's measured faces land.

rows.label: Total transferred JS on a settled report route, incl. lazy chunks
rows.enforcedBy: WO-21 -- a Playwright network-transfer assertion on a settled report route, in the per-PR chromium job
rows.definition: Lazy chunks are fetched at runtime, so this row CANNOT be derived from the build manifests (WO-23 criterion 4). It is carried here so the ceiling has a single home and is visible in budget-report.md, explicitly marked as not gated by npm run budgets.

rows.label: Derived: total first-load transfer for `/c/[id]`, cold cache
rows.definition: JS + CSS + fonts. A transfer ceiling, not an LCP ceiling: fonts load font-display: swap, are cached across both routes, and do not block first paint.
